# Future Directions — The Topology of Knotted Light

This cycle established the topological charge of an orbital-angular-momentum beam
as an additive invariant governed by a contour-integral **product rule**
`w(φ·ψ) = w(φ) + w(ψ)`, showed the charge is carried by the full physical
amplitude (not merely its phase), and bridged the charge of a torus-knot beam to
the arithmetic `lcm` of its knot parameters. The following conjectures extend
these findings.

## 1. The winding number is a group homomorphism onto the integers
**Conjecture.** The map sending a non-vanishing, piecewise-smooth beam loop to its
winding number is a surjective group homomorphism from the multiplicative group of
such loops onto `(ℤ, +)`, and its kernel is exactly the loops that lift to a
single-valued logarithm over one turn.
**The key insight is** that additivity of charge is not a property of the
exponential ansatz but of the logarithmic derivative, so *every* admissible beam —
however it is engineered — obeys the same conservation law.
**Why now?** With the product rule proved for general loops, the remaining step is
only to identify the kernel with the exact (globally-integrable-logarithm) loops,
a self-contained analytic characterization.

## 2. Torus-knot beams realize every meridional charge, and coprime pairs are extremal
**Conjecture.** Among all `(p, q)` torus-knot beams with fixed charge `N = p·q`,
the coprime factorizations are exactly those whose singularity is a single
connected knot rather than a split link; equivalently, `gcd(p,q)` counts the
connected components of the phase singularity.
**The key insight is** that the arithmetic identity `lcm p q = p·q ⇔ gcd(p,q)=1`
is the shadow of a topological dichotomy (knot vs. link) at the level of the beam's
zero set.
**Why now?** The charge/`lcm` bridge is in hand; the next move is to promote the
scalar identity to a statement about the number of components, which is a finite,
checkable combinatorial invariant.

## 3. Annihilation is the only way to lower total charge
**Conjecture.** For any finite family of beams, the total winding number of their
superposition equals the sum of charges, and it can be strictly reduced only by
including beams of opposite handedness whose singularities pairwise cancel; no
continuous, singularity-free deformation changes the total.
**The key insight is** that the winding number is a homotopy invariant of the loop
in `ℂ \ {0}`, so charge is conserved unless a zero is created or destroyed.
**Why now?** Conservation over families is already proved as a contour-integral
corollary; upgrading it to a homotopy-invariance statement connects it to the
standard degree theory of the punctured plane.

## 4. Charge quantization survives radial and polarization dressing
**Conjecture.** Multiplying a beam by any nowhere-zero, single-valued envelope
(radial profile, Gaussian waist, or scalar polarization factor) leaves the winding
number unchanged; hence the integer charge is a robust label independent of the
experimentally uncontrolled amplitude.
**The key insight is** that only the phase's failure to be single-valued
contributes to the contour integral, so any genuinely single-valued dressing is
invisible to the invariant.
**Why now?** The special case of a constant envelope (and the `r^{|ℓ|}` Laguerre–
Gauss factor) is already proved; the general envelope case needs only the same
logarithmic-derivative cancellation applied to an arbitrary non-vanishing factor.

# Future Directions: Analogy as an Adjoint Operation

This cycle recast analogy-making between two ordered structures as the taking of an
*adjoint pair* `(forward, backward)` bound by the adjunction law
`forward a ≤ b ↔ a ≤ backward b`. The round-trip `backward ∘ forward` was shown to be a
closure operator (inflationary, monotone, idempotent), the backward map was shown to be
uniquely determined by the forward map, and the structural fidelity — the number of source
points recovered exactly by a round trip — was shown to be maximized precisely by *perfect*
analogies. The canonical best analogy for a min-plus (tropical) map was identified with
its max-plus residual, recovering the classical shortest-path reconstruction inequalities.
The following conjectures push these findings further.

## 1. Fidelity is a rank-type invariant of the analogy

**Conjecture.** For an analogy over a finite source, the fidelity (number of round-trip
fixed points) equals the size of the image of the closure operator `backward ∘ forward`,
and this quantity is monotone under composition of analogies: the fidelity of a composite
analogy never exceeds the smaller of the two component fidelities.

The key insight is that the fixed-point set of the fidelity operator is exactly the set of
"analogically stable" concepts — those that survive translation unchanged — so counting
them is the same as measuring the rank of the stabilized sublattice, and rank can only
drop when analogies are chained.

Why now? We have already established that the round trip is an idempotent closure operator,
so its image is well defined and equals its fixed-point set; the remaining step is to show
this image size behaves submultiplicatively under composition, which is a finite, checkable
combinatorial statement rather than an open-ended search.

## 2. Best analogies are Lipschitz-optimal reconstructions

**Conjecture.** Among all backward maps paired with a fixed forward map, the adjoint
backward map minimizes the worst-case reconstruction defect measured in the natural
sup-metric; moreover, in the tropical setting this optimal defect is controlled by the
spread of the matrix entries along each column.

The key insight is that the residual is not merely *a* left inverse but the *tightest*
over-approximation permitted by monotonicity, so any competing backward map must pay a
strictly larger reconstruction error somewhere, and in the min-plus world that error is
exactly a difference of column extrema.

Why now? The adjunction inequalities `w ≤ A ⊗ (A♯ w)` and `A♯ (A ⊗ v) ≤ v` proved this
cycle already sandwich the reconstruction; converting the sandwich into a sharp Lipschitz
bound only requires the sup-inf inequality already available in the tropical toolkit.

## 3. Perfect two-way analogies are exactly order isomorphisms of the stable cores

**Conjecture.** Every analogy restricts to a perfect two-way analogy — an order
isomorphism — between the image of its source-side closure operator and the image of its
target-side interior operator, and this restricted isomorphism is the unique maximal
sub-analogy that loses no structure.

The key insight is that even a lossy analogy hides a perfectly faithful core: the closure
and interior operators carve out exactly the sublattices on which forward and backward are
mutually inverse, so every analogy is an isomorphism "up to stabilization."

Why now? This cycle proved that a two-sided perfect analogy is an order embedding and that
the round trips are idempotent; the images of those idempotents are the candidate cores,
so the conjecture is the natural completion of results already in hand.

## 4. Analogical composition forms a category with residuation as inverse

**Conjecture.** Analogies between ordered structures compose associatively, identities are
the trivial self-analogies, and the perfect analogies are exactly the isomorphisms of the
resulting category; in the tropical instantiation, composition of analogies corresponds to
min-plus matrix multiplication and residuation reverses the arrows.

The key insight is that the adjunction law is preserved under composition, so "being an
analogy" is a closed, categorical property, and the tropical residual furnishes a concrete,
computable dagger-style involution on the arrows.

Why now? The uniqueness of the backward map established this cycle guarantees composition is
well defined on the forward maps alone, removing the main obstruction to organizing analogies
into a category.

## 5. Fidelity concentration for random tropical analogies

**Conjecture.** For a min-plus matrix with independent random entries, the fidelity of the
canonical analogy on the discretized source concentrates sharply around a deterministic
value determined only by the entry distribution and the dimension, with fluctuations
vanishing as the dimension grows.

The key insight is that whether a source point is a round-trip fixed point depends only on
local column comparisons, so fidelity is a sum of weakly dependent indicator variables and
should obey a law-of-large-numbers-style concentration.

Why now? The exact characterization of round-trip fixed points proved this cycle turns
fidelity into an explicit counting statistic, making it amenable to the standard
concentration machinery for sums of nearly independent indicators.

# Future Directions — Colorful Carathéodory with polynomial-size witnesses

This cycle established a two-parameter picture of *witness complexity* for the
colorful Carathéodory phenomenon: a face capturing the target point can always be
certified inside a sub-complex whose face count is polynomial of degree `k+1` in
the number of vertices, and this collapses to linear when the certifying complex is
a spanning tree (`k = 1`). The captured face itself was produced on the line from
the honest convex-hull hypotheses. Below are conjectures that extend these
findings.

## 1. Sharp linear witnesses for every fixed width
**Conjecture.** For every fixed `k`, a spanning `k`-tree on `n` vertices has a
face count that is *linear* in `n`, namely at most `2^{k} · (n - k) + (2^{k+1} - 1)`,
strictly below the degree-`k+1` bound that holds for arbitrary width-`(k+1)`
complexes.

The key insight is that the generic degree-`k+1` bound is driven by *width alone*,
whereas a `k`-tree also carries global acyclicity: each newly attached vertex
contributes a bounded number of new cliques, so the total grows additively rather
than combinatorially. Why now? The `k = 1` case is already settled here (the exact
`2n` count for trees), and it isolates acyclicity as the mechanism responsible for
the collapse; the general `k` statement is the natural inductive lift of that one
mechanism.

## 2. Rainbow capture inside a spanning tree of the join
**Conjecture.** For colour classes on the line whose hulls all contain the origin,
one can pre-select a spanning tree of the join `V₁ * V₂` — of only linearly many
edges — that is guaranteed to contain a rainbow edge through the origin, so the
exponential join never needs to be examined.

The key insight is that the origin-capturing edges are not scattered arbitrarily:
they form a "crossing" pattern determined by the sign pattern of the two colour
classes, and a single monotone matching of nonpositive to nonnegative points meets
this pattern. Why now? The existence half is proved here via the sign-extraction
lemma, which already exhibits *one* crossing edge; upgrading "one edge exists" to
"a linear pre-committed tree always contains one" is the decisive next step toward
algorithmic witnesses.

## 3. Higher-dimensional sign extraction
**Conjecture.** In `ℝ^d`, if the origin lies in the convex hull of a finite colour
class `V`, then `V` contains an affinely independent sub-family of at most `d+1`
points whose hull already captures the origin, and this Carathéodory sub-family can
be located by examining only polynomially many `(d+1)`-subsets when the search is
restricted to a spanning `d`-tree of `V`.

The key insight is that the one-dimensional argument — extract a nonpositive and a
nonnegative element via the extreme points `min'`, `max'` — is the shadow of a
general extreme-point selection: the origin's barycentric coordinates are supported
on a bounded face, and spanning-tree structure controls how many candidate faces
must be probed. Why now? The planar base case is complete and pinpoints extreme
points as the extraction device; the machinery for finite-dimensional convex hulls
needed to iterate it is exactly the classical Carathéodory support argument.

**Conjecture.** The degree-`k+1` polynomial witness bound is asymptotically tight:
there exist width-`(k+1)` complexes (the full `≤(k+1)`-skeleta) whose face count
matches `∑_{i≤k+1} C(n,i)` up to a constant factor, so no sub-polynomial witness

removing acyclicity restores the full skeleton, whose exact count `∑_{i≤k+1} C(n,i)`

is fresh.

theorem insert_apex_injective {v : α} {σ : Finset α} (hv : v ∉ σ) :

  intro τ hτ;
  simp_all +decide [ Finset.ext_iff ];
  grind

`2^k` new faces: one for every bit-vector/subset of the attaching face.

  rw [ coneFaces, Finset.card_image_of_injOn ];
  · rw [ Finset.card_powerset ];

  simp_all +decide [ Finset.disjoint_left, coneFaces ];
  grind

    (hK : ∀ τ ∈ K, τ ⊆ ground) :
    (K ∪ coneFaces v σ).card = K.card + 2 ^ σ.card := by
